## Goal

**As** a project owner scaffolding agent guidance from this repository, **I want** `templates/project-AGENTS.md` to carry the project-level conventions that audits actually enforce, **so that** a new project inherits the two rules that a 2026-10-29 cross-project audit session had to invent on the spot instead of discovering them late.

Discovered-from: `WL-0MVR8EXR6009F05V` (ContextHub) — an epic audit that returned `Ready to close: No` on an acceptance criterion the producer had already decided to accept, and an `implement` run whose push gate did not run the suite the skill documentation says it runs.

## Scope note (read before implementing)

The definite "the template" is taken to mean **`templates/project-AGENTS.md`** — the canonical project `AGENTS.md` seed consumed by `scripts/init_project_agents.py` (see `docs/dev/project-agents-md.md`). That file is deliberately minimal ("reference structure only"), so this item **adds project-level guidance sections, not a copy of the global rules**.

If the intent was instead the framework sources (`skill/audit`, `skill/report`, `skill/implement`) rather than the project template, re-scope this item before implementing — the framework findings are listed at the end as separate, unfiled work.

## Problem

Two conventions were needed during the ContextHub epic and neither is documented for a project owner:

1. **Recording a producer-accepted acceptance-criteria variance.** The producer decided to accept one AC without the last piece of live evidence. The audit runner ignores `wl auditWaiver` entirely (`grep -n waiver skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` → no matches); the *only* way to make an audit score that criterion `adjusted` (non-blocking) instead of `partial` (blocking) is to write the accepted variance into the criterion's own text in the work-item description, resolve the recorded open question, and *additionally* record `wl audit-waive` so the closure guard and `wl doctor audit-gaps` agree. Done that way, the epic audit returned `Ready to close: Yes` with the criterion `adjusted`, a clean Phase 1/Phase 2 (`calls=2 parse_ok=2`). Done any other way it silently stays blocking and the item ping-pongs between implement and audit.
2. **Declaring the project's real push gate.** `skill/implement` and `skill/audit` both state that the dev-push pre-push hook enforces the full suite (`run_tests.py --scope full`). That is true only where the v3 hook is installed: this repository ships `.githooks/pre-push` (v3, with the scope-aware test gate), but a project seeded earlier (ContextHub) still runs `worklog:pre-push-hook:v2`, which enforces branch policy, the context budget and worklog sync **and nothing else**. Green test evidence therefore came from the `implement.py finish` full-scope run, not the hook. A project owner needs to be told to assert this, because the failure mode is silent: pushes succeed and the cached full-suite evidence the audit consumes read-only never exists.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `templates/project-AGENTS.md` gains a `## Recording an accepted acceptance-criteria variance` section stating the three-step procedure — (a) amend the criterion's text in the work-item description with an explicit "Accepted variance (producer decision, <date>)" clause naming what evidence stands in for the missing evidence, (b) resolve the corresponding open question in the item description, (c) record `wl audit-waive <id> --reason "<why>"` — and explains **why** the description is mandatory (the audit runner scores an AC from its text and ignores `auditWaiver`).
- AC2: The same template gains a `## Declaring your push gate` section telling a project owner to verify which pre-push hook version the project actually runs (`git config core.hooksPath` + the `worklog:pre-push-hook:vN` banner line) and to record the answer in the project's own guidance, so the full-suite evidence an audit consumes is known to exist (or is known to come from `implement.py finish` instead of the hook).
- AC3: `docs/dev/project-agents-md.md` is updated to match — it must describe the template as carrying these two optional guidance sections and stay truthful about the "reference structure only, never a copy of the global rules" constraint; `scripts/init_project_agents.py` output must remain idempotent (re-running never duplicates the reference or the new sections).
- AC4: A test pins the guarantee: emitting a fresh project `AGENTS.md` via `scripts/init_project_agents.py` produces a file containing both new sections, and re-running it is a no-op (`scripts/init_project_agents.py --dry-run --json` reports no change).
- AC5: The two conventions stay project-scoped: no global workflow rule is duplicated into the template (the global layer remains `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` via `scripts/install_pi.sh`), and `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` is re-measured only if the template changes the always-loaded surface.
- AC6: Full project test suite passes with the new changes (enforced by the dev-push gate).

## Key Files

- `templates/project-AGENTS.md` — the canonical project `AGENTS.md` seed; the two new sections go here.
- `scripts/init_project_agents.py` — the installer that reads the template (`TEMPLATE_PATH`) and must stay idempotent.
- `docs/dev/project-agents-md.md` — the installer documentation to keep in sync (it quotes the canonical file verbatim, so the quoted block must be updated too).
- `tests/` — wherever the installer's tests live (`grep -rln "init_project_agents" tests/`), for the AC4 pin.

## Constraints

- Do **not** copy global agent rules (workflow, wl lifecycle, coding disciplines) into the template — that duplication was removed by `SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G` and must not come back.
- Project-specific guidance stays project-specific: both new sections are conventions a *project owner* opts into, not new global mandates.
- Keep the installer idempotent and its output deterministic; no new dependency.
- UK English; match the existing Markdown style of the file and its quoted copy in the docs.

## Related findings from the same session (not in this item's scope — file separately if wanted)

1. `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` maps an AC verdict of `adjusted` to `unmet` in its Acceptance Criteria table (it only knows `met`/`unmet`), so a *passing* audit that carries an accepted variance renders as `❌ failed` with an `unmet` row. The report had to be corrected by hand.
2. `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py start` fails (`ERROR: Failed to create worktree …`) when a feature branch with the expected name still exists but its worktree directory was removed; the operator has to `git worktree add <path> <branch>` manually and re-run `start` (which then resumes idempotently).
3. `skill/audit` in-main-slot mode (default) emits `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` child screens that, when unserviced, produce a `Ready to close: No` whose AC rows are all `partial` **and** persist partial child audits that later block the parent — `--no-child-in-main-slot` was the only path that produced a usable report in three consecutive runs.
data.title: Carry the accepted-variance and push-gate conventions into templates/project-AGENTS.md

# implement.py start: nested node_modules symlink blocks submodule init (bootstrap ordering)

**Discovered from:** RISE-0MVRZKINX004HNEE (tce-the-rising implement run, 2026-10-29).

## Problem

`implement.py start` initialises submodules *after* it creates the
`node_modules` symlinks. When a submodule's own root has a `node_modules` in
the main checkout (tce-the-rising's `core` submodule does), the nested-symlink
pass creates `<worktree>/core/node_modules` inside the still-**empty**
submodule directory. `git submodule update --init` then cannot clone into
`core/` and fails:

```
fatal: clone of 'file:///home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine' into submodule path '…/core' failed
fatal: destination path '…/core' already exists and is not an empty directory.
```

Because submodule init failures are deliberately fail-open (SA-0MSN52GGN002B0AZ
AC2), `start` only logs a warning and the session proceeds with an
**uninitialised submodule**: `npm run build` (`tsc --noEmit`) then dies with
`Cannot find module './core/scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin'`,
`@core-engine/SaveLoad`, etc. Every child session in that worktree must
hand-fix the checkout before it can build.

Secondary defect: even after a successful init, the symlink is not ignored by
the submodule's `.gitignore` (`node_modules/` has a trailing slash, which does
not match a *symlink*), so the superproject reports `M core` and the worktree
looks dirty.

## Evidence

- Call order in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (start phase):
  `_ensure_node_modules_symlink` (≈L4608) → `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks`
  (≈L4614) → `_ensure_submodules` (≈L4618).
- Observed on tce-the-rising worktree
  `wl-RISE-0MVRZKINX004HNEE-…`: `git submodule status` showed
  `-19f30ac… core` (uninitialised) while `core/` contained only the
  `node_modules` symlink; the first `npm run build` produced ~40 `TS2307`
  errors from the missing submodule.
- Manual fix that worked: `rm core/node_modules && rmdir core`,
  `git -c protocol.file.allow=always submodule update --init --recursive`,
  re-create `core/node_modules`, and add `node_modules` to the submodule's
  `info/exclude` (the trailing-slash pattern in `core/.gitignore` does not
  match the symlink).

## Required change

- Run `_ensure_submodules` **before** the node_modules symlink passes, or make
  the nested-symlink pass skip paths that are inside an
  uninitialised/unchecked-out submodule (a gitlink with an empty directory).
- Make the worktree's `git status` clean after the symlinks are created: drop
  or neutralise the symlink's untracked status (e.g. immediately cover it by
  an exclude entry, or create the nested link only after init and add the
  path to the worktree's exclude).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A worktree whose submodule root has a `node_modules` in the main checkout is
  fully initialised by `start`: `git submodule status` in the worktree shows a
  checked-out submodule (no leading `-`) and the repo's build succeeds.
- Ordering regression test: fixture repo with a local-path submodule plus a
  `<submodule>/node_modules` in the main checkout → after `start`, the
  submodule is checked out at the recorded commit and the worktree
  `git status --porcelain` is clean.
- The fail-open contract is unchanged: a genuinely failing
  `git submodule update` still only logs a warning and does not abort `start`.
- No behavioural change for repos without submodules or without a submodule
  `node_modules`.
- `implement/SKILL.md` submodule section notes the ordering constraint.

## Constraints

- Do not remove the node_modules symlinking feature itself
  (SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B) — only fix its ordering/ignoring relative to
  submodules.
- Keep the change generic; no tce-the-rising / `core`-specific hardcoding.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_ensure_submodules`,
  `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks`, start-phase call order.
- `skill/implement/tests/` — ordering/regression test next to
  `test_implement_submodules.py`-style fixtures.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — submodule documentation.
data.title: implement.py start: nested node_modules symlink blocks submodule init (bootstrap ordering)

## Problem statement

The ship skill's audit gates declare an `in_review` work item blocking while
reporting the reason `Ready to close` — a self-contradictory verdict — because
the content-fingerprint fast path silently never fires (the `check-freshness`
probe is invoked with an unsupported `--json` flag and its error is swallowed by
a fail-open `catch`), and in-gate remediation cannot restamp an audit that the
runner itself considers fresh. The result is a release that cannot proceed on a
passing audit with no actionable remedy short of a ~13-minute forced re-audit.

## Users

**Release operator** (runs `/skill:ship release` and reads the gate report):

> As a release operator, when every `in_review` item's audit content is
> unchanged since it was audited, I want the ship gates to treat that audit as
> current — no matter that `wl sync` moved `updatedAt` afterwards — so a release
> is never blocked by a passing audit whose only "staleness" is a timestamp.

> As a release operator reading a blocking report, I never want to see a
> blocking item whose reason says it passed; if the gate really must block, I
> want the reason to name the actual condition and give me a command that fixes
> it.

**Skill maintainer** (owns `skill/ship/scripts/`):

> As a maintainer, I want the gate→runner contract pinned by tests that assert
> the exact invocation shape, so a flag drift between `check-audit-gate.js` and
> `audit_runner.py` cannot silently degrade the fast path again.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **The content-freshness probe actually runs.** Either
   `audit_runner.py check-freshness <id> --json` is accepted by the runner's
   subparser (preferred: additive, matches the CLI already documented in
   `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/ship/SKILL.md` and
   `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`), or the JS call sites stop
   passing `--json`. A unit test asserts the parsed-argument shape
   (`["check-freshness", "SA-1", "--json"]` parses, `command ==
   "check-freshness"`) **and** asserts the exact command string built by
   `queryContentFreshness()` stays in sync with it, so the two sides cannot
   drift apart again.
2. **A time-stale passing audit is upgraded by both gates.** A hermetic
   (injected-boundary) unit test proves that a `fresh: true` response
   turns a time-stale **passing** audit into a non-stale, non-blocking,
   non-remediated item in **both** `check-audit-gate.js`
   (`checkAuditReadyToClose`) and `check-final-validation.js`
   (`checkFinalValidation`) — including through the real
   `queryContentFreshness()` JSON parse, not only a stubbed
   `queryContentFreshnessFn`.
3. **No contradictory block after in-gate remediation.** A post-remediation
   status of `{passing: true, stale: true}` never produces `status:
   'blocking'` with reason `Ready to close`. The shared remediation path
   (`attemptAuditRemediation()`, used by the audit gate, the final-validation
   sweep and `refresh-audits.js`) re-queries content freshness and
   (a) returns `passing` with a reason naming the content-fresh basis when the
   fingerprint is unchanged, or (b) blocks with a reason that names the real
   condition (`time-stale but content changed`) plus the actionable remedy
   `audit_runner.py issue <id> --force`. An invariant test asserts no blocking
   entry is ever emitted with reason `Ready to close`.
4. **Regression test for the observed sequence.** A hermetic test reproduces
   the ContextHub failure exactly — audit `readyToClose: true`, `auditedAt` <
   `updatedAt`, v2 fingerprint present and unchanged, and a remediation
   `issue <id>` run that short-circuits (exits 0 leaving a passing but
   time-stale audit) — and asserts the gate does **not** block the release
   (item lands in `remediatedItems`/passes, exit status not 6/12).
5. **Docs state the contract.** `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`
   (where the content-fingerprint fast path is documented) and this repo's
   ship reference `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` both state that (i)
   content-fresh audits are trusted regardless of `updatedAt`, and (ii) an
   in-gate remediation that returns a passing-but-time-stale audit must not
   block. The `--json` flag for `check-freshness` is documented as supported.
6. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **No `--force` in the happy path.** The gate must not force a genuine
  re-audit (~13 min) merely because `updatedAt` moved; `--force` appears only
  as the documented remedy when content genuinely changed.
- **Preserve fail-open safety.** A probe failure must still fall back to the
  conservative time gate — never silently pass a stale audit.
- **Stay hermetic in tests.** No live `wl`/`audit_runner` invocations; reuse the
  existing injected boundaries (`runAuditShow`, `runAuditCommand`,
  `resolveAuditRunnerFn`, `queryContentFreshnessFn`, `createRemediationBudgetFn`).
- **One shared implementation.** The fix belongs in `attemptAuditRemediation()`
  / `queryContentFreshness()`, not duplicated in `check-final-validation.js`
  (Game-Scenes/Gym-Scenes parity principle: shared logic, not copies).
- **Do not weaken existing gates.** A genuine fresh failing verdict, a missing
  audit, or a content-changed audit must still block; `--skip-audit-remediation`
  semantics are unchanged.
- **Scope discipline.** The `audit_runner.py` `issue` short-circuit
  behaviour itself is out of scope (it is correct: it refuses to re-audit fresh
  content); record any further runner improvements as separate work items.

## Existing state

- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`
  - `queryContentFreshness()` (line ~442) builds
    `python3 "<runner>" check-freshness <id> --json` and swallows failures into
    `{fresh: false}`.
  - `checkAuditReadyToClose()` (line ~750) applies the fast path only when
    `status.stale && hasContentFingerprint(auditData)`, then remediates.
  - `attemptAuditRemediation()` (line ~643) runs `issue <id>` (no `--force`),
    re-reads `wl audit-show`, and blocks when
    `status.isBlocking || status.transient || status.stale` — this is where
    `{passing: true, stale: true}` becomes `blocking` with reason
    `Ready to close`.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` mirrors the fast path
  (`classifyAudit`, ~line 630) and imports the shared
  `attemptAuditRemediation`/`queryContentFreshness`.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `check-freshness` subparser (line
  ~14933) accepts only `issue_id` and `--worklog-dir`; it always prints JSON.
  `cmd_issue` short-circuits a fresh audit (line ~10341) printing
  `Skipping: audit still fresh — Ready to close: Yes` and returning 0 without
  restamping `auditedAt`.
- Verified in this session: `audit_runner.py check-freshness <id> --json` →
  `error: unrecognized arguments: --json` (exit 2); without `--json` it prints
  the expected JSON (exit 0).
- Existing coverage does not catch either defect: JS tests inject
  `queryContentFreshnessFn` (bypassing the command string);
  `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py` parses
  `["check-freshness", "SA-1"]` without `--json`.

## Desired change

1. `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`: accept `--json` on the
   `check-freshness` subparser (output is already JSON), documented as accepted
   for compatibility with the ship gates.
2. `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`:
   - keep the command string and the runner parser in sync, pinned by tests;
   - extend `attemptAuditRemediation()` to accept an injectable
     `queryContentFreshnessFn`: when the post-remediation status is
     `passing && stale` **and** `hasContentFingerprint(auditData)`, probe
     content freshness — fresh → `status: 'passing'` with a content-fresh
     reason; not fresh/legacy/fingerprint-less → `status: 'blocking'` with
     reason naming `time-stale but content changed` and the
     `audit_runner.py issue <id> --force` remedy;
   - never emit a blocking entry whose reason is `Ready to close`.
3. `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js`: rely on the shared
   remediation fix (no duplicated logic); only adjust its report wording if
   needed for the new reason text.
4. Tests: extend `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`,
   `tests/unit/test-check-final-validation.mjs` (regression + invariant) and
   `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py` (`--json` parses).
5. Docs: update the contract paragraphs in
   `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` and
   `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`; confirm `skill/ship/SKILL.md` Step-2
   wording still matches (it already claims the read-only probe runs).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — sync the probe command with the
  runner; teach `attemptAuditRemediation()` to resolve
  `passing + stale` by content freshness instead of blocking.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` — shared-remediation consumer;
  verify the fast path and post-remediation wording.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — accept `--json` on the
  `check-freshness` subparser.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py` — pin the accepted
  argument shape.
- `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs` — command-shape, upgrade and
  regression/invariant tests.
- `tests/unit/test-check-final-validation.mjs` — mirrored fast-path and
  regression tests.
- `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — content-freshness contract
  (fast path + post-remediation).
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — mirrored contract statement.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — verify Step-2 wording matches the fixed behaviour.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — `check-freshness --json` now accurate.

## Related work

- **SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI** (completed) — introduced the content-fingerprint fast
  path this item repairs; its tests inject the probe so they never exercise the
  real command.
- **SA-0MUOO5UEB008RXBP** (completed) — shared staleness semantics between the
  Step-2 gate and the Step-3.7 sweep; the `passing: true, stale: true` state
  that produces the contradictory block comes from this sharing.
- **SA-0MVIDICGZ0030DXC** (completed) — `hasContentFingerprint()` v2-prefix
  detection (unchanged by this work).
- **SA-0MUOO5V0P00461X8** (completed) — bounded in-gate remediation; the
  contradiction is currently masked behind the budget logic.
- **SA-0MUOO5WV0006D7UD** (completed) — `--skip-audit-remediation`; that flag
  also blocks on this state, so the fix must reach it.
- **SA-0MUOO5TRU005ALBL**, **SA-0MUOO5VMH005VF69** (completed) — earlier
  stale-audit false-block elimination this item continues.
- **SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0** (completed) — item-data-only fingerprint semantics.
- Duplicate check: searched `audit gate freshness ship release` +
  `content fingerprint stale`; no completed item satisfies these ACs (all
  candidates predate and cause the defects) — this is a follow-up fix, not a
  duplicate.

### Related work (automated find-related report)

- **SA-0MRJBEJGY0095XAY** – Add recent-audit gate to audit skill startup
  (completed)
- **SA-0MSQJABHZ0018APE** – Content-gate child verdict reuse in parent audits
  (completed)
- **SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT** – Audit: content-based freshness gate (completed)

Repository file matches: `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`,
`docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (all confirm the
probe/contract locations named in **Key Files**).

## Related docs

- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` (Step 2 audit readiness gate)
- `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` (fast-path paragraph, line ~188)
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` (Step 2/3.7 gate descriptions)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (`check-freshness` read-only probe)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (`_check_audit_freshness`,
  `cmd_check_freshness`)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** fixing the probe consistently may make the remediation path
  redundant for content-fresh items, so tests asserting "remediation attempted"
  counts will need updating. *Mitigation:* keep the existing budget/limit tests
  and add the new expectation alongside.
- **Risk:** a runner-side `--json` flag that is accepted-but-ignored could hide
  future output-format drift. *Mitigation:* pin the emitted JSON shape in the
  runner test and assert `queryContentFreshness()` parses it.
- **Risk:** reason-text changes break report-format tests. *Mitigation:* grep
  for `Ready to close` assertions before editing wording.
- **Risk (scope creep):** the audit runner's `issue` short-circuit and the
  remediation budget are tempting refactor targets. *Mitigation:* they are out
  of scope; file separate work items if improvements are spotted.
- **Assumption:** accepting `--json` in the runner is preferred over removing
  it from the JS, because four documentation locations and this repo's audit
  reference already document `check-freshness <id> --json` (additive, no
  doc-churn, and it hardens the CLI against exactly this class of drift).
- **Assumption:** updating both `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`
  and `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` is in scope, because existing tests
  (`tests/unit/test-ship-skill.mjs`) already assert these docs mirror each
  other on ship behaviour.
- **Assumption:** no producer decision is needed to proceed — the item body
  already fixes the root cause, ACs and preferred remedy direction.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Which side of the `--json` mismatch should be fixed — the runner or the
  JS call sites? — **Answer (Map, intake session, no producer answer required):**
  accept `--json` on the runner subparser. **Evidence:** `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`,
  `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` and
  `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py` docstring already
  document `check-freshness <id> --json`; a live run confirms the flag is
  rejected (`unrecognized arguments: --json`, exit 2) while output is already
  JSON. Preferred option recorded; the alternative (strip `--json` from the JS)
  remains valid if the implementer prefers it, provided AC1's sync test exists.
- **Q:** May the gate block a passing-but-time-stale audit after remediation
  (AC2 option b), or must it always unblock (option a)? — **Answer (Map, intake
  session):** prefer (a) unblock when the content fingerprint is unchanged, and
  fall back to (b) only when content changed, since (a) removes the false block
  while (b) keeps genuine content-changed audits gated with an actionable
  `--force` remedy.
- **Q:** Is `refresh-audits.js` in scope? — **Answer (Map, intake session):** yes,
  implicitly — it consumes the shared `attemptAuditRemediation()`, so no
  separate changes are planned beyond keeping its tests green.
- **Q:** Should the audit runner's `issue` short-circuit be changed to restamp
  `auditedAt`? — **Answer (Map, intake session):** no. Restamping without a
  re-audit would falsify the audit timestamp; the gate must instead honour the
  runner's content-freshness verdict. Recorded as out of scope.


## Implementation notes (implementation session, 2026-10-30)

**Outcome: no source change was required.** All seven acceptance criteria were already delivered by the four child items on `dev`; this session's work was to prove that and repair the evidence path the audit reads.

**Root cause of the audit's AC5/AC6 `partial` verdicts: a stale main checkout.** Local `dev` pointed at `0e3c406b3`, a content-identical duplicate of origin's `701625a9b` (both patch-ids `8a0f4702617b0160380411fd92c738a354b41ff5`), so it lacked the documentation commit `b7296e652` even though that commit was already on `origin/dev`. Audit evidence is read from the main checkout's working tree, so the content-freshness contract paragraphs appeared absent. The pre-sync tip was preserved as `refs/heads/backup/local-dev-0e3c406b3` and local `dev` was advanced to `origin/dev`; the duplicate's content is identical, so nothing was lost.

**Verification at the pushed tree (`a91334fe7`, `origin/dev`).**
- Full project suite green: 5265 passed, 14 skipped, 12 xfailed, 0 failed (pytest) plus all node suites (unit / node / cli) green — executed through the test skill, so the audit consumes it from cache.
- Contract present and pinned: `Content-freshness contract (SA-0MVTU2643004QTQN)` in `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` and `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`, the explicit "passing-but-time-stale must not block" rule in `skill/ship/SKILL.md` Step 2, and `check-freshness <id> --json` documented in `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`; `tests/unit/test-ship-skill.mjs` pins the two references together.
- `implement.py finish` completed on the no-diff push path with the post-push ancestry assertion satisfied.

**Assumption recorded.** No acceptance-criterion text was changed; only this notes section was appended, deliberately, so the item-data-only (v2) content fingerprint is recomputed and a full verification audit runs against the repaired checkout instead of short-circuiting on the stale "No" verdict.

## Problem statement

The refactor scan filed this item as a critical `unused_import` finding (ruff `F811`, "Redefinition of unused `implement_mod`") against a worktree copy of `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`. That finding has **already been silenced** — commit `c39cb4454` added five line-scoped `# noqa: F811 — fixture param, not a redefinition` comments — so `ruff check` on `dev` is currently clean. What remains is the suppression noise itself: five separate "this is not a redefinition" assertions, each attached to a different line in the same file, when the intent belongs at exactly one place — the import. A single explicit re-export at the import site expresses that intent once and removes all five suppressions.

## Users

- **Test maintainer / agent** editing `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`: wants the fixture-sharing intent stated once, at the import, instead of re-verified against five inline suppressions.
- **Code reviewer / audit agent**: wants ruff clean without suppressions that require per-line re-justification.
- **Future test author** borrowing another test module's fixture: wants a precedent in this repo for re-exporting a fixture cleanly.

User stories:

- As a test maintainer, I want the fixture re-export declared once at the import so that the five `# noqa: F811` comments can be deleted without ruff complaining.
- As a reviewer, I want the lint result to stay clean when the suppressions are removed, so trust in the lint gate is preserved.
- As a future test author, I want a documented pattern for reusing a fixture defined in another test module.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` imports the fixture with an explicit re-export alias (`implement_mod as implement_mod`) and the file contains **zero** `# noqa: F811` comments — verify: `grep -c "noqa: F811" tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` returns `0`, and `grep -n "implement_mod as implement_mod" tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` returns the import line.

The repo lint gate reports no findings for this file and no new findings elsewhere — verify: `ruff check tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` reports zero findings, and the gate's own entry point (`from code_review.scripts.linter_runner import run_ruff`, as used by the code-review tests) returns no findings for this path.

4. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments (the module docstring/comment explaining fixture reuse), README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Do not relocate fixtures** into `tests/conftest.py` (or a shared fixtures module) as part of this item — that is a larger, higher-blast-radius change. Record it as a linked follow-up if it looks worthwhile.

## Existing state

- Finding origin: refactor scan of the now-deleted worktree `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MVLJXKB60088SND-tests-drive-recovery-test-harness-termin/` (the ephemeral path is dead; the live file is `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`).

# Dev-push full-suite gate: bind the verdict to the pushed commit (cache-subject hardening)

## Problem statement

The dev/main pre-push gate (`.githooks/pre-push` → `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env`) derives its cache key from the repository state of the directory git runs the hook in — the **main checkout** — and never from the `<local_sha>` being pushed. When a green `scope: full` entry already exists for that main-checkout state, the gate is satisfied instantly and no suite executes for the pushed tree, so a red commit can reach `dev` on another tree's verdict.

The **pusher-side** half of this defect (`implement.py finish` pushing from `repo_root` instead of the worktree that holds the commit) is owned by epic **SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3**. This item owns the **gate-side** half: the pre-push verdict must be attributable to the pushed commit, and a cache entry computed from any other state must never satisfy it — regardless of which tool performed the push.

## Users

- **AI agents running `/skill:implement`** — rely on "the dev push succeeded" meaning "the full suite ran against what landed".
- **Producers / release operators** — rely on the invariant *landed on `dev` ⇒ full suite green at that commit* when approving a finish or a release.
- **Auditors / reviewers** — consume the cached full-suite entry at the pushed commit as evidence (`run_tests.py --summary`, audit F3 `query_cached()`).
- **Pushers outside the implement workflow** — manual `git push … :dev`, ship/release tooling, or any future automation that pushes from a checkout that is not the pushed commit.

User stories:

- "As an agent finishing work, when my commit is pushed to `dev` I expect the gate to have executed the suite at **my** commit — or the push to be refused — never to inherit another tree's green verdict."
- "As a producer, I expect a gate pass to prove the pushed tree was tested, so 'green on dev' is trustworthy even when the main checkout is dirty or parked on a different commit."
- "As an auditor, I expect the gate's green entry to be keyed on the pushed commit's state so `--summary`/`query_cached` can attest it."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Gate subject is the pushed commit.** `.githooks/pre-push` forwards the pushed `<local_sha>` to the suite gate, and the full-suite gate validates a checkout of **that commit with no dirty paths** — never the main checkout's unrelated `HEAD`/dirty state. (Design detail in *Desired change*.)
2. **No cross-tree cache hit.** A `scope: full` entry recorded for any other state — including a green entry for the main checkout's own state — cannot satisfy the gate for the pushed commit; on a miss the full suite executes for the pushed tree. A genuinely red pushed tree still blocks the push.
3. **Verdict provenance is attributable.** The gate records/emits the state it validated (resolved project root, `HEAD` sha / pushed sha, cache `git_state` and `fingerprint_kind`, executed-vs-cached) on the hook's `stderr`, and the green entry left behind is a **worktree-kind `scope: full`** entry at the pushed commit's state so Step-9 `--summary` and audit F3 can consume it.
4. **Fails closed with an actionable message.** When the pushed commit cannot be gated (sha not present locally, no checkout holds it, or the only candidate checkout is dirty in a way that changes its state), the hook refuses the push and names the sha, the remote ref, the remedy, and the `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` escape hatch — it never silently gates a different tree.
5. **Regression tests** (no wall-clock proxies; cache hits driven by staged entries):
   - a green `scope: full` entry for the main checkout's state does **not** satisfy the gate for a different pushed commit (the suite executes, and the state validated is the pushed commit's);
   - a green entry keyed on the pushed commit's clean state **is** served as cached, with `git_state`/`fingerprint_kind` matching;
   - a dirty push cwd parked on the pushed sha still gates the clean pushed tree;
   - an unmaterialisable pushed sha refuses the push and runs no suite.
6. **Documentation updated**: `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` (cache-fingerprint contract — the pre-push gate becomes a subject-bound consumer, removing "pre-push" from the "callers that pass nothing keep worktree keys" list), `skill/test/SKILL.md` (gate semantics), `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` (release-gate row), plus `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` wherever they describe the gate's subject or the worktree/`wl sync` interaction.
7. **Cross-project hook propagation recorded and applied.** `core.hooksPath=.githooks` makes the hook a **per-project file**; the change is applied here and the verified list of checkouts that need the same edit is recorded (SorraAgents, AI_Hell, ContextHub, dev-scripts, llm-manager, Tableau-Card-Engine per the epic's rollout inventory), including any deliberate divergence.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No weakening.** `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` remains the only escape hatch; the default path never fails open, and a red pushed tree is still refused.
- **Cache compatibility.** Keys stay the existing worktree-kind `git_state` (`compute_git_state` = `HEAD` sha + dirty-content hash) + suite command; no new key namespace, no `compute_git_state` behaviour change, and existing entries at the pushed commit stay reusable **and audit-visible**. (A tree-kind fingerprint — the finish gate's staged-tree binding — is deliberately *not* used for the gate: `query_cached()` is a worktree query, so a tree-kind entry would be invisible to Step-9/audit F3.)
- **Hook is per-project** (`core.hooksPath=.githooks`), so the edit must be propagated explicitly; the runner-side change reaches every project through the global skill install.
- **Worklog sync behaviour unchanged.** The hook already skips `wl sync` for linked-worktree pushes; the gate must not introduce a sync from inside a pushed worktree, and `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` stays the documented bypass.
- **Cost bound.** The gate may execute one full suite for a pushed commit that was never gated (that is the point); it must not execute more than one, and must reuse an existing green entry at the pushed commit.
- **Repo boundary.** The hook and `run_tests.py` changes land here; other projects' hook copies are touched only as recorded in AC7.
- **No wall-clock timing proxies** in tests — drive executed-vs-cached with staged cache entries (see `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`).

## Existing state

- `.githooks/pre-push` (v3) parses `<local_ref> <local_sha> <remote_ref> <remote_sha>` from stdin but uses only `remote_ref`; the gate invocation is `python3 "$runner" --scope full --strict-git-env --json`, run with the hook's cwd, so the cache key comes from `compute_git_state(cwd)` — the main checkout.
- `run_tests.py` has **no CLI way to name the gated commit** (only `--project-root`, `--scope`, `--type`, `--strict-git-env`, `--target-branch`). The `fingerprint=` override (`run_suite`/`run_all`/`guarded_run_all`/`run_cached`) exists only on the Python API used by `implement.py finish` (`gate_index.tree`).
- `skill/test_cache.py` already records `fingerprint_kind` (`"worktree"`/`"tree"`) and `lookup()` misses a different kind or a different state; `compute_tree_state()` and `FINGERPRINT_KIND_TREE` exist (SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB).
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` § *Cache fingerprint contract* explicitly states that callers passing no fingerprint keep historical worktree keys — naming "test-skill CLI, audit, **pre-push**" as unbound consumers. That sentence is the contract this item changes.
- Existing regression harness: `tests/test_pre_push_test_gate.py` runs the hook end-to-end in a throwaway repo with a fake recording runner; `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py` and `tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py` cover runner/cache behaviour.
- Observed instance (this item's origin): `finish` pushed `bf1fb2921` to `origin/dev` with the gate "satisfied" in seconds; a detached checkout of that commit reported **no** cache entry (`git_state 14300398…`), while the only recent green `scope: full` entries were keyed on the main checkout's state (`git_state c3e34f77…`, main `dev` at `d23fb4503` plus a dirty `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`). See *Evidence* below.

## Desired change

The gate must know **which commit it is gating** and must bind its cache lookup to a checkout of that commit.

- **Option A (recommended).** `.githooks/pre-push` passes the pushed `<local_sha>` as a new `--gate-commit <sha>` (name TBD) to `run_tests.py`. The runner resolves the subject: (i) the push cwd itself when its `HEAD` equals the sha **and** it has no dirty paths; else (ii) a checkout listed by `git worktree list` whose `HEAD` equals the sha and which is clean (this is exactly the pusher's worktree after the epic's fix, so the normal path is a cheap in-place run); else (iii) refuse the push with the actionable message from AC4. The suite then runs (or is served from cache) under that root, so the cache key is the pushed commit's clean state. No temporary worktree is created, so suite dependencies (`node_modules`, virtualenvs) stay as the pusher installed them.
- **Option B.** Option A plus a fallback that materialises the commit in a temporary detached worktree when no clean checkout holds it. Stronger coverage, but a fresh worktree usually has no installed dependencies, so suite commands may fail for reasons unrelated to the pushed tree — treat as a producer choice, not the default.
- **Option C.** Reinstate strict in-place gating: refuse the push whenever the push cwd's `HEAD` ≠ pushed sha **and** the tree is dirty, without searching for another worktree. Simplest, but rejects manual pushes from a clean main checkout even when the pusher's worktree is available.

All options keep the existing red-suite refusal and `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` bypass, and keep the `--project-root`/`--scope`/`--strict-git-env` contract intact for every other caller.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.githooks/pre-push` — forward `<local_sha>` to the gate; keep the worklog-sync and branch-policy sections untouched.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — new `--gate-commit` flag, subject resolution (in-place / worktree lookup / refusal), provenance line on stderr, cache key from the resolved root; must not alter default (no-flag) behaviour.
- `skill/test_cache.py` — only if a worktree-kind explicit fingerprint or entry lookup helper is needed; prefer no change (keys must stay worktree-kind).
- `tests/test_pre_push_test_gate.py` — extend the existing hook harness (marker file records the runner argv; assert the pushed sha is forwarded).
- `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py` (or a new `tests/test_pre_push_gate_subject.py`) — cache-subject regression tests (AC5).
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`, `skill/test/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`, `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — gate-subject and cache-contract documentation.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3** (epic, `plan_complete`) — pusher-side fix: push from the worktree that holds the commit, fail-closed subject guard, gate evidence. Its rollout child **SA-0MVUTXKKP0005DWS** explicitly names this item: *"`SA-0MVTRBT50005DUEH` is narrowed to its remaining gate-side gap (§Desired change option 3 — refuse a cache hit whose git_state was not computed from the pushed tree), which this item's scope discipline keeps out of scope"*. Sibling children: SA-0MVUTXILY003DVTE (regression tests), SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN (worktree push), SA-0MVUTXJM8006PQY4 (evidence), SA-0MVUTXK41000FC08 (docs).
- **SA-0MVV1V1DB0035Q6B** (open) — the same gate-side defect observed on 2026-10-30 (~27 s push window, no full-scope entry written); its ACs (pushed-tree refusal, verdict attribution, green push leaves an entry at the pushed state, regression test) overlap this item's AC1–AC5 heavily. See **Q1**.
- **SA-0MVU0IS9S006BFE3** (open) — same root cause for the first-attempt path; the epic's rollout child plans to close it as satisfied once the pusher-side fix lands.
- **SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB** (completed) — tree-fingerprint cache binding: added `compute_tree_state()` / `fingerprint_kind` / explicit-fingerprint override that this item reuses where appropriate and deliberately does not use for the gate (evidence visibility).
- **SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2** (completed) — finish-gate provenance precedent (gate the tree the commit produces).
- **SA-0MUH9R74O002MQDU**, **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** — push timeout / flake handling; the gate-subject change must not extend push time unboundedly or make retries ambiguous.
- **MS-0MVM7NJF70037YU4** — origin (`discovered-from`).
- Code/docs: `.githooks/pre-push`, `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `skill/test_cache.py`, `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` § *Cache fingerprint contract*, `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` § release-gate table, `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, `skill/implement/SKILL.md` Step 9.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — hook drift across projects.** Six checkouts use `core.hooksPath=.githooks` with known pre-existing hook divergence; the fix only protects a project whose hook forwards the pushed sha. Mitigation: AC7's verified list; the runner-side flag is inert until a hook passes it.
- **Risk — evidence visibility.** The cache is per repo root (`cache_dir(repo_root)`), and no mirroring exists in the tree (`mirror_suite_cache` referenced by the epic's plan is **not** present in code — see Q7). If the gate runs in the pusher's worktree, its entry lands in that worktree's cache and is invisible to the main checkout's Step-9 `--summary`/`query_cached`. Mitigation: run in place when possible; otherwise write/mirror the entry to the main checkout's `.worklog/cache` (coordinate with the epic's rollout child) or record the gap explicitly.
- **Risk — extra suite cost.** A pushed commit never gated before now executes a full suite at push time (observed ~10–12 min). Intended, but the hook must not run twice and must surface progress; the push-timeout handling from SA-0MUH9R74O002MQDU must still apply.
- **Risk — false refusals.** A push whose commit exists only on the remote, or from a shallow clone, cannot be gated locally; the refusal message must be clear and name `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`. Assumption: pushing a commit that is not present locally is already impossible for a normal `git push`.
- **Risk — scope creep.** "Make the hook trustworthy" invites rewriting branch policy, context-budget and worklog-sync sections; those stay untouched. Extra opportunities (e.g. hook-side evidence parity with the epic's pusher-side evidence) are recorded as linked work, not scope.
- **Assumption.** The pusher-side epic lands first (dependency edge), so the normal `implement.py finish` path is a cheap in-place gate and this item is defence-in-depth for manual/other-tool pushes.
- **Assumption.** `compute_git_state` remains path-independent, so an entry created by the gate in one checkout is reusable for the same commit in another checkout of the same repo.

## Evidence

- `/tmp/ms-finish.log` (finish + push phase) and `/tmp/ms-rerun.log` (an independent full run at `bf1fb2921`: 5121 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failures), host 2026-10-29.
- Main-checkout cache entry `.worklog/cache/5242612354ca965b6c6724d2d196e432` (`git_state c3e34f77…`) versus the pushed commit's `git_state 14300398…`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Overlap with `SA-0MVV1V1DB0035Q6B` ("Dev-push full-suite gate did not execute for the pushed commit"): keep both items or fold?** — **OPEN QUESTION (producer).** That item's ACs (pushed-tree refusal even when the main checkout is cached-green; verdict attributable to the pushed commit; green push leaves an entry at the pushed state; refused-fast-forward regression test) are largely the same work as this item's AC1–AC5. **Recommended:** keep this item as the concrete mechanism slice (it is the one the epic's plan already narrows to the gate-side remainder) and close `SA-0MVV1V1DB0035Q6B` as satisfied when this lands, recording the landed commit there — rather than implementing the same change twice. Evidence: both descriptions and AC lists; `SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3` Appendix Q7; `SA-0MVUTXKKP0005DWS` AC4.
- **Q2 — How should the gate materialise the pushed commit: Option A (in-place or existing worktree, else refuse), Option B (A + temporary detached worktree fallback), or Option C (strict in-place only)?** — **OPEN QUESTION (producer).** **Recommended:** Option A — it gates the exact pushed commit without creating a checkout that lacks the pusher's installed dependencies, and it matches the epic's producer answer that the pushed tree is gated transparently when materialisable and the push fails closed otherwise (epic Appendix Q2). Evidence: `.githooks/pre-push` stdin contract; `git worktree list` availability; dependency-installation risk in fresh worktrees.
- **Q3 — Is a per-project `.githooks/pre-push` change acceptable, given the epic deliberately avoided hook edits because of cross-project drift?** — **OPEN QUESTION (producer).** **Recommended:** accept it — the pushed sha is only available to the hook (git passes it on stdin), so the gate cannot learn its subject any other way; propagate to the six known checkouts and record the verified list (AC7). Alternative if rejected: scope the change to this repository's hook and record the residual exposure for the other projects, which leaves them on today's behaviour. Evidence: epic Appendix Q5 rationale; `git config core.hooksPath` inventory recorded in `SA-0MVUTXKKP0005DWS`.
- **Q4 (resolved by research) — Is the cache key path-dependent, i.e. could a gate run in a worktree fail to reuse an entry created in the main checkout?** — No. The key is `command + git_state (+ test_type)`; `git_state` is `sha256(HEAD + porcelain dirty content)` and `--project-root` is not part of it. Evidence: `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` § *Cache fingerprint contract*; `skill/test_cache.py::compute_git_state` / `cache_key`.
- **Q5 (resolved by research) — Does the pusher-side epic alone close this item?** — No. It removes the main trigger for agent-driven finishes, but a manual/other-tool push from a checkout whose `HEAD` ≠ the pushed sha is still gated against the wrong tree, and the hook still never reads `<local_sha>` (it parses the line and discards it). Evidence: `.githooks/pre-push` test-gate section; epic description's scope-discipline clause.
- **Q6 (resolved by research) — What did the epic's plan already decide about this item?** — Narrow it to the gate-side cache-refusal remainder; close `SA-0MVU0IS9S006BFE3` as satisfied; keep gate-side hardening out of the epic's scope. Evidence: `SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3` Appendix Q7 and its Plan changelog; `SA-0MVUTXKKP0005DWS` AC4.
- **Q7 (resolved by research; cross-item finding) — Is the cache entry a worktree run creates visible to the main checkout's Step-9/audit path?** — No, as the tree stands today: `cache_dir(repo_root)` resolves per root (`.worklog/cache`, else the root's git dir), and no mirroring helper exists — `mirror_suite_cache`, cited by the epic's plan and `SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN`'s cache-compatibility AC, is absent from `skill/`, `.githooks/` and `scripts/`. Consequence: an entry written by a gate running in a pusher's worktree would be invisible to the main checkout's `run_tests.py --summary` and audit F3 until mirrored. Recorded here for the epic's rollout child (`SA-0MVUTXKKP0005DWS`); this item will either run in place (main checkout holding the pushed commit) or mirror the entry.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN** – Push to dev from the worktree that holds the commit (blocked)
- **SA-0MVUTXJM8006PQY4** – Surface dev-push gate evidence on success (blocked)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0mvl2nh1g0094fa2, 0mvm7njf70037yu4, 0mvqhvhxi007pqab, absent, ac1 (+439 more)

# `implement.py parent`/`drive` start children whose status is `blocked` — re-validate the block before starting or skipping

Discovered-from: **MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6** (tce-main-street) — producer decision Q3 (2026-10-29): *"yes, though it should first check that the block is still valid"*.

## Goal

As an implement agent running an epic, I need `implement.py parent`/`drive` to never start a child that is deliberately `blocked` unless the block no longer holds, so a verification child is not implemented against a prerequisite that has not landed and I am not asked to fabricate its evidence.

## Problem statement

`phase_parent()` classifies children with `_classify_child()` (`implement/scripts/implement.py:874`): terminal → `skip-terminal`, `in-progress` → `skip-in-progress`, **everything else → `implement`**. Status `blocked` therefore falls through to `implement`.

Blocker awareness exists but does not gate the start:

- `_in_chain_blockers()` only considers blockers that are **themselves children of the same parent** (`implement.py:5920-5975`), so a child blocked on anything outside the parent's children set is startable.
- `external_blockers` is populated from outbound `wl dep` edges only (`implement.py:5771-5790`) and is reported as a "coordination note". It is `[]` when the block is recorded in prose instead of as a dependency edge — which is how cross-project blocks are written (`**Blocked by (SorraAgents):** SA-…` in the child description).

**Live evidence (this item's origin):** on 2026-10-29 `implement.py parent MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` started child `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4` — status `blocked`, unblock condition "`SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2` is in `dev`/`in_review`", which was still `open`/`intake_complete` — created a worktree and reported `external_blockers: []`. The child had to be aborted (`implement.py abort`, worktree removed) to avoid producing unverifiable AC evidence.

The inverse failure matters too: a **stale** block must not strand a child forever. Once the blocker lands, the child must become startable again (or its status refreshed) rather than being skipped silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A child whose `status` is `blocked` is never started while its block still holds: `_classify_child()` (or the caller) yields a distinct `skip-blocked` outcome, and the child is reported in `children_processed` with its blocking ids — not started, not `skipped-in-progress`.
- [ ] **Re-validation of dependency-edge blocks:** for a `blocked` child the outbound `wl dep list` edges are resolved; the block is **stale** iff every blocker is terminal (`completed`/`done`/`in_review`) or soft-deleted, in which case the child is startable again (and the stale block is named in the report/log). Any non-terminal blocker holds the block.
- [ ] **Re-validation of cross-project and prose blocks:** blocker IDs declared in the child description's `Blocked by …` line (and/or a machine-readable `externalBlockers` field, whichever is implemented) are collected and surfaced in `external_blockers`; an unresolvable cross-project id holds the block and is reported with an actionable message (id + where to check it), never silently ignored and never silently startable.
- [ ] A block that cannot be validated (no dep edges, no parseable blocker line, unknown status) is treated as **holding** and reported as unvalidated — it must not default to startable.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: (a) `blocked` + open external blocker → not started, reported with ids; (b) `blocked` + blocker now terminal → stale block detected and child started; (c) `blocked` + no resolvable blocker → not started, message names the unresolved id; (d) `drive` propagates the same classification/report fields; (e) existing in-chain sibling ordering, cycles and terminal/in-progress behaviour unchanged (regression cases).
- [ ] Live evidence recorded on this item: re-running `implement.py parent MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` (three `blocked` verification children) starts nothing and reports all three with their `SA-…` blockers.
- [ ] `implement/SKILL.md` "Guards" list gains the blocked-child re-validation rule (stale blocks are re-evaluated, not honoured forever), and the parent-recursion section documents the new report vocabulary.
- [ ] Node and pytest suites green for the changed framework code (run through the test skill / finish gate, never an ad-hoc runner).

## Constraints

- Do not weaken the existing guards: dependency order, cycle fail-fast, "never re-implement terminal children", "never clobber another agent's `in_progress` claim", and `--finalise-stranded` semantics stay as they are.
- No change to `implement.py start`/`finish` single-item behaviour; this is the parent/`drive` fan-out classification only.
- Cross-project resolution must stay fail-open in the sense that an unresolvable id reports clearly and does not crash the phase — it just holds the block.
- Prose parsing must not become the only mechanism: prefer declared dependency edges, and keep the prose path narrowly scoped to an explicit `Blocked by` line.

## Key Files

- `implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_classify_child()`, `phase_parent()` (child classification, `_in_chain_blockers`), `phase_drive()` (report propagation), `wl_dep_blockers()`.
- `implement/scripts/tests/` (or the repo's existing implement test location) — new unit tests for the classification matrix.
- `implement/SKILL.md` — Guards + parent recursion report vocabulary.
- Reference cases: `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` children `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4`, `MS-0MVTEVKOD002OKSO`, `MS-0MVTEVL4Z009LUUR`, `MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1` (all `blocked`, blockers in prose).

## Related work

- `SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2`, `SA-0MVL7YOMJ006UMDO`, `SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z` — the three blockers of the origin item's verification children.
- `SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T` — introduced `external_blockers` as coordination notes; this item makes them gate the start.

---

## Plan (plan skill, 2026-10-30)

**Headline:** Split the fix into a test-first contract item, three vertical
behaviour slices (classification → prose/cross-project blockers → drive
reporting), a docs item and a live-evidence item, all under this parent, with
every parent AC mapped to a child.

### Child work items (test-first, dependency order)

| # | Id | Title | Type | Effort/Risk |
|---|----|-------|------|-------------|
| C1 | `SA-0MVUTD3IX004E03C` | Tests: blocked-child classification matrix for parent/drive | task | M / Medium |
| C2 | `SA-0MVUTD408005OFNW` | phase_parent: classify a still-blocked child as `skip-blocked` (dep-edge re-validation) | feature | M / Medium |
| C3 | `SA-0MVUTD4HS000O6AB` | Prose `Blocked by` and cross-project blockers hold a blocked child | feature | M / Medium |
| C4 | `SA-0MVUTD4ZD006O4N5` | phase_drive: propagate `skip-blocked` classification and blocker ids | feature | S / Low |
| C5 | `SA-0MVUTD5GQ004V6UO` | Docs: `implement/SKILL.md` guards + parent-recursion report vocabulary | docs | XS / Low |
| C6 | `SA-0MVUTD5YF001PLOF` | Live evidence: `parent MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` starts no blocked child | task | S / Medium |

Dependency edges (all wired with `wl dep add`):

```
C1 (tests, no blockers)
 └─ C2 ─┬─ C3 ─┬─ C4 ─┬─ C5 (docs)
        │      │      └─ C6 (live evidence)
        └──────┴────────┘
```

Ordering rationale: C1 writes the red contract first (parent AC 5); C2 lands
the dep-edge verdict (AC 1, 2, 4-dep-path); C3 adds the prose/cross-project
path (AC 3, 4-prose-path) and makes the fail-closed default actionable; C4
propagates the verdict through `drive` (AC 1 "reported in `children_processed`"
on the drive path); C5 documents the shipped vocabulary (AC 7); C6 produces the
live evidence (AC 6). Each slice is end-to-end: code + tests + the finish gate.

### Parent AC → child coverage

| Parent AC | Covered by |
|---|---|
| AC1 `skip-blocked` distinct outcome, reported in `children_processed` with blocking ids | C2 (classification + report), C4 (drive propagation), C1(a) |
| AC2 dep-edge re-validation, stale iff every blocker terminal/soft-deleted | C2, C1(b) |
| AC3 prose `Blocked by` / cross-project ids surfaced in `external_blockers`; unresolvable holds with an actionable message | C3, C1(c) |
| AC4 unvalidatable block holds and is reported unvalidated | C2 (no dep edges), C3 (no parseable line) |
| AC5 unit tests (a)–(e) | C1 |
| AC6 live evidence on `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` | C6 |
| AC7 `implement/SKILL.md` Guards + report vocabulary | C5 |
| AC8 node + pytest suites green through the test skill / finish gate | every child's finish gate; stated explicitly in C1 and C2 |

### Assumptions (recorded, not invented requirements)

- **A1 — test location.** The Key Files section above predicted
  `implement/scripts/tests/`; the repo's existing implement tests live in
  `tests/test_implement_*.py` at the repo root, so C1 creates
  `tests/test_implement_parent_blocked_child.py` there.
- **A2 — prose only, no schema change.** AC3's "and/or a machine-readable
  `externalBlockers` field, whichever is implemented" is satisfied by parsing
  the explicit `Blocked by …` line plus declared dependency edges; no `wl`
  schema change (wl is a separate ContextHub-owned CLI).
- **A3 — cross-project ids are resolvable in principle.** `implement.py`
  already routes `wl` calls through
  `shared/status_lifecycle.resolve_worklog_flags`, whose prefix-to-sibling scan
  maps an id prefix to its owning project's worklog. Verified on 2026-10-30:
  from `/home/rgardler/projects/tce-main-street`, prefix `SA` resolves to
  `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.worklog` and `MS` to the tce worklog.
  Whether C3 *uses* that to detect a landed cross-project blocker is Q3 below.
- **A4 — one existing test encodes the superseded contract.**
  `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py::TestParentDependencyOrder::test_external_blocker_reported_not_started_early`
  asserts that a `blocked` child with an out-of-chain blocker **is started**
  ("coordination notes" per `SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T`). This item deliberately
  supersedes that behaviour; C1 updates and renames the test rather than
  leaving two contradictory contracts.
- **A5 — legacy helper kept.** `_next_child_to_implement()` has no production
  call site (only `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py`); C2 keeps it
  consistent with the new rule instead of deleting it (dead code is reported,
  not removed, in a bug-fix slice).
- **A6 — the live-evidence run can start something.** The origin epic's AC1
  child `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4` is `open` (not `blocked`) with
  `assignee: Map` + tag `do-not-delegate`; `phase_parent` honours neither
  (that is `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876`, itself `blocked`). See Q1.
- **A7 — `blocked` status writes are unreliable.** `WL-0MVTUKSJZ003WK82`
  (ContextHub) records `wl update --status blocked` reporting success while the
  stored status reverted to `open`; the classification must therefore never
  depend on the framework being able to *write* `blocked`.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-30 — initial plan: 6 children created (`SA-0MVUTD3IX004E03C`,
  `SA-0MVUTD408005OFNW`, `SA-0MVUTD4HS000O6AB`, `SA-0MVUTD4ZD006O4N5`,
  `SA-0MVUTD5GQ004V6UO`, `SA-0MVUTD5YF001PLOF`), 11 dependency edges wired,
  six automated review stages run, AC coverage verified at 100 %.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Round 1 (2026-10-30, plan skill, downtime dispatch — **no interactive
producer available**; questions recorded here and flagged for producer review).

- **Q1 — What is the scope of the live-evidence AC (AC6)?**
  The origin epic `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` now has **three** `blocked` children
  (`MS-0MVTEVKOD002OKSO`, `MS-0MVTEVL4Z009LUUR`, `MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1`) and one
  **`open`** child (`MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4`) held only by `assignee: Map` + the
  `do-not-delegate` tag. `phase_parent` honours neither assignee holds nor
  `do-not-delegate` (that is `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876`, itself `blocked`), so the
  post-fix run will still start that open child — while AC6 as written says the
  run "starts nothing".
  Options: **(A)** scope AC6 to "none of the three `blocked` children is
  started, all three reported `skip-blocked` with their `SA-…` ids", and report
  the open held child truthfully with a cross-reference to
  `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876`; **(B)** widen this item to also gate on
  `do-not-delegate`/assignee holds (overlaps `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876`, which is
  already planned and blocked); **(C)** prove the behaviour on a synthetic
  fixture epic in this repo and record the MS run as pending until
  `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876` lands.
  **Recommended:** A — it proves exactly the bug this item owns (a `blocked`
  child is never started) without duplicating the do-not-delegate item, and
  keeps the live evidence honest about what the run did.
  **Answer:** **OPEN QUESTION** — directed to the producer. Why it matters: it
  decides whether C6 (`SA-0MVUTD5YF001PLOF`) can be executed at all, and
  whether the MS epic stays held after this fix lands.

- **Q2 — When a block is found stale, should the child's lifecycle status be
  refreshed, or only the start allowed?**
  AC2 says the child "is startable again (and the stale block is named in the
  report/log)"; the Goal paragraph adds "(or its status refreshed)".
  Options: **(A)** start the child and report/log the stale block, leaving the
  `blocked` status to the lifecycle owner (a comment on the child records the
  stale finding); **(B)** also flip the child to `open` via `StatusLifecycle`
  with an audit comment before starting; **(C)** flip to `open` and clear the
  prose `Blocked by` line.
  **Recommended:** A — it never silently erases a producer-set hold, it keeps
  `phase_parent` a reader of lifecycle state rather than a writer of it, and
  `WL-0MVTUKSJZ003WK82` shows blocked-status writes are unreliable in `wl`.
  **Answer:** **OPEN QUESTION** — directed to the producer. Why it matters: it
  determines whether C2 mutates child status (and therefore whether it needs
  the `StatusLifecycle` audit-comment path).

- **Q3 — Should a cross-project prose blocker be resolved through the sibling
  worklog scan (so a landed external blocker makes the block stale)?**
  `resolve_worklog_flags` already maps an id prefix to its owning project's
  worklog (verified for `SA` → SorraAgents and `MS` → tce-main-street), so
  resolution is technically available without any network call.
  Options: **(A)** resolve cross-project ids through that scan: terminal →
  stale (child startable), non-terminal → holds, and only a genuinely
  unresolvable id holds as unvalidated; **(B)** do not resolve cross-repo —
  every cross-project id holds, and the child's owner must refresh the child
  when the external item lands; **(C)** resolve opportunistically (try the
  scan, fall back to holds) but never cache the result.
  **Recommended:** A — it is what makes the origin epic self-unblocking when
  the three `SA-…` items land, which is the inverse failure the Goal names
  ("a stale block must not strand a child forever"); B leaves three MS
  children stranded forever and contradicts that Goal.
  **Answer:** **OPEN QUESTION** — directed to the producer. Why it matters: it
  changes C3's acceptance criteria (and its tests) materially.

All three questions are recorded on this item as a comment and the item is
flagged `needsProducerReview`. Planning itself is complete and independent of
the answers; only C6 (Q1), the status-refresh behaviour in C2 (Q2) and the
cross-project resolution in C3 (Q3) depend on them.

# implement.py pushes from the main checkout, so the pre-push full-suite gate can validate the wrong tree (and be cache-served)

> **Intake outcome (2026-11-01): reconciled as a scope-duplicate — do NOT implement here.**
> Every acceptance criterion below is owned by the existing epic
> **SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3** and its children (with the gate-side residual owned by
> **SA-0MVTRBT50005DUEH**), and the epic's rollout child
> **SA-0MVUTXKKP0005DWS** already carries the AC *"`SA-0MVU0IS9S006BFE3` is
> closed as satisfied (its AC1–AC4 are met by this item) once the fix has landed
> on `dev`"*. This item is therefore retained only as the discovery record:
> intake is complete, it is dependency-blocked on the epic, and its closure is
> owned by the rollout child. See **Coverage and duplicate decision**.

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` performs the dev push with
`git_push_to_dev(repo_root, branch, commit_hash)` — from the **main checkout**,
not the worktree that holds the commit being pushed. The `.githooks/pre-push`
full-suite gate then resolves its runner, `--project-root` and cache key from
that push cwd (`repo_root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"`), so the suite
either runs against the main checkout's `HEAD`/dirty state or is **served from a
cache entry recorded for that other state**. A commit that was never tested can
therefore land on `dev` on another tree's green verdict.

## Users

- **AI agents running `/skill:implement`** — "the dev push succeeded" must mean
  "the full suite ran against what landed".
- **Producers / release operators** — rely on *landed on `dev` ⇒ full suite
  green at that commit* when approving a finish or a release.
- **Auditors / reviewers** — consume the cached `scope: full` entry at the
  pushed commit as evidence (`run_tests.py --summary`, audit F3).

User stories:

- "As an agent finishing work, when my commit is pushed to `dev` I expect the
  gate to have executed the suite at **my** commit — never to inherit another
  tree's green verdict."
- "As a producer, I expect a gate pass to prove the pushed tree was tested, so
  'green on dev' is trustworthy even when the main checkout is dirty or parked
  on a different commit."
- "As an auditor, I expect a green entry keyed on the pushed commit's state."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The dev-push full-suite gate evaluates the tree being pushed (the pushed
   commit), not the main checkout's `HEAD`/dirty state — e.g. push from the
   worktree, or run the gate against the pushed commit via a temporary worktree
   / explicit `--project-root` at that commit.
2. A regression test pins it: a dev push whose committed tree differs from the
   main checkout's `HEAD` cannot be satisfied by a cache entry recorded for the
   main checkout state (assert the gate's cache key / executed state is the
   pushed commit).
3. Documentation for the dev-push gate (``skill/test/SKILL.md``,
   ``skill/implement/SKILL.md``, ``docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md``) states
   which tree is validated.
4. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No weakening.** `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` stays the only escape hatch; the default
  path never fails open and a red pushed tree is still refused.
- **Cache compatibility.** Full-suite evidence stays keyed by suite command +
  git state (`HEAD` sha + dirty-content hash), so entries created for the pushed
  commit stay reusable **and audit-visible**; no new key namespace.
- **Cost bound.** The gate may execute at most one full suite for a pushed
  commit that was never gated.
- **Repo boundary.** Any change lands in SorraAgents; per-project
  `.githooks/pre-push` copies need explicit propagation and must be recorded.

## Existing state (verified against `dev`, 2026-11-01)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` still pushes from the main checkout:
  `git_push_to_dev(repo_root, branch, new_commit)` in the non-fast-forward
  recovery (`:6658`, inside `_recover_non_fast_forward_push`) and
  `git_push_to_dev(repo_root, branch, commit_hash)` in `phase_finish` Step 6
  (`:7180`). The pusher-side fix (SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN) has **not** landed.
- `.githooks/pre-push` (v3) derives `repo_root="$(
  git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` and runs
  `python3 "$runner" --scope full --strict-git-env --json` with no
  `--gate-commit`; it parses `<local_sha>` from stdin and discards it. The
  llm-manager copy additionally passes `--project-root "$repo_root"` and calls
  `mirror_suite_cache "$repo_root"` (pre-existing per-project drift).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` exposes no `--gate-commit`; the full-suite
  cache key comes from `compute_git_state(cwd)` — the push cwd's `HEAD` sha plus
  a dirty-content hash (`skill/test_cache.py`).
- The 2026-10-31 field comment on this item quotes a pusher-side refusal
  (`pre-push gate refuses this push: the tree it would measure is not the pushed
  commit`). **That guard is not present anywhere in current code** — a repo-wide
  grep of `.githooks/`, `skill/`, `scripts/` and `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/`
  finds it only in the worklog DB. The failure is real but the guard appears to
  have come from an unmerged worktree or a since-reverted hook copy, so the
  observed cannot-recover loop is not reproducible from `dev` today. Recorded
  here as evidence for the epic's rollout verification.
- Observed instance (this item's origin, 2026-10-29): a push completed in 18 s
  (commit `c34fd7d91`, 19:54:44 → `origin/dev` 19:55:02) where a full suite
  takes ~12 min, and no cache entry existed for the pushed commit's clean-state
  fingerprint (`67451abcabf1301b`); the only recent entries belonged to a
  concurrent finish. The commit was independently verified green

## Goal

As an agent running the changed-scope test gate, I want a changed `tests/unit/test-*.mjs` file to select the node suite for that directory, so a JS/TS test edit is actually executed before commit instead of only at the push-time full suite.

## Problem

`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::_is_test_file()` recognises `test_*.py`, `*_test.py`, `*.test.mjs` and `*_test.mjs` but **not** the repo's dominant node convention `test-*.mjs`. Consequences:

1. A changed `tests/unit/test-*.mjs` file is not classified as a test file, so `map_changed_to_tests()` tries the convention mapping instead (`test_<stem>.py` etc.) and selects nothing.
2. The same filter builds the `all_tests` pool used by import-graph expansion, so `test-*.mjs` files can never be selected there either.
3. Emission of a node command requires a selected `.mjs` path, so no `node --test` command is produced at all.

Verified while delivering SA-0MVTU1WHS002HN1C: editing three test files (`skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py`, `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`, `tests/unit/test-check-final-validation.mjs`) produced a changed-scope command containing only `pytest ...` — no `node --test`. 43 of the 44 `tests/unit/*.mjs` files use the `test-` prefix, so the gap covers almost the whole node unit suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `_is_test_file()` recognises `test-*.mjs` (and the equivalent `test-*.js`/`test-*.ts` naming already used by `tests/unit`) as test files.
- A unit test asserts that changing a `tests/unit/test-foo.mjs` file selects `tests/unit/test-foo.mjs` and causes a `node --test` command to be emitted by the changed-scope command builder (no pytest-only command).
- The selection never invents a path that does not exist (the existing LP-0MTZYRTNF0092JKW existence filter still applies).
- Existing changed-scope selection tests stay green; the full suite stays green.

## Constraints

- Do not widen selection to arbitrary `.mjs` helper files (e.g. `cli-helpers.mjs`); only the test-file naming conventions.
- Keep the single-source-of-truth rule: one filter function, no duplicated naming logic.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`
- `skill/test/tests/`

## Related work

- discovered-from:SA-0MVTU1WHS002HN1C (observed while adding hermetic ship-gate tests).

# Tests: blocked-child classification matrix for `implement.py parent`/`drive`

Parent: **SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2** (*implement.py parent/drive start children whose status is blocked — re-validate the block before starting or skipping*).

**Test-first contract item.** Write these tests **before** the implementation
items C2 (`skip-blocked` via dep-edge re-validation), C3 (prose/cross-project
blockers) and C4 (`drive` propagation). They are expected to be **red** until
those land — they are the executable form of the parent's ACs 1–5.

## Goal

As an implement agent, I need an executable contract for how a child whose
`status` is `blocked` is classified, reported and (not) started, so that the
fix cannot silently regress and a stale block can never strand a child forever.

## Context (read before writing tests)

- `_classify_child()` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, ~line 1127)
  currently returns `skip-terminal` / `skipped-held` / `skip-in-progress` /
  `implement`. **`blocked` falls through to `implement`** — the defect.
- `phase_parent()` (~line 6609) populates `external_blockers` from outbound
  `wl dep` edges only and reports it as a coordination note; it never gates
  the start. `phase_drive()` (~line 7934) already re-propagates
  `blocked_children` from the parent report.
- The live failure: on 2026-10-29 `implement.py parent MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6`
  started child `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4` (status `blocked`, blocker in prose) and
  created a worktree; the child had to be aborted.
- Harness patterns to reuse: `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py`
  (`ParentHarness`, mocked `wl_show` / `wl_show_children` / `wl_dep_blockers` /
  `phase_start` / `_invoke_implement` / `_discover_worktree` /
  `StatusLifecycle.update_status` / `wl_add_comment` /
  `is_code_freeze_active`) and `tests/test_implement_drive.py`
  (`ScriptedParent` + `RecordingSpawner`).
- `wl show --children --json` already returns each child's `description` and
  `tags`, so prose blockers need no extra fetch; `wl dep list <id> --json`
  returns `outbound` entries carrying `id` and `status`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unit tests cover: (a) `blocked` + open external blocker → not started, reported with ids; (b) `blocked` + blocker now terminal → stale block detected and child started; (c) `blocked` + no resolvable blocker → not started, message names the unresolved id; (d) `drive` propagates the same classification/report fields; (e) existing in-chain sibling ordering, cycles and terminal/in-progress behaviour unchanged (regression cases).
- [ ] New module `tests/test_implement_parent_blocked_child.py` (pytest, module-scoped `implement_mod` fixture loading `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`; harness reused from `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py`, not re-implemented).
- [ ] **(a)** `blocked` child + **non-terminal** dep-edge blocker → child **not** started; its `children_processed` entry carries `action: "skip-blocked"` with `blocking_ids` naming the blocker, and is neither `skip-in-progress` nor `skipped-terminal`.
- [ ] **(b)** `blocked` child whose **every** dep-edge blocker is terminal (`completed` / `done` / `in_review`) or soft-deleted → **stale block** detected, child started, and the stale block is named in the report (e.g. `stale_blocks` / a message naming the blocker).
- [ ] **(c)** `blocked` child whose blocker is declared only in prose (a `**Blocked by (SorraAgents):** SA-…` line) with no dep edge and an id that cannot be resolved in this worklog → **not** started, and the report/message names that id together with where to check it (actionable, not silently ignored, not silently startable).
- [ ] **(d)** `phase_drive` propagates the same classification and blocker fields: no session is spawned for a `skip-blocked` child, and the drive report carries the child id plus its blocking ids (in `blocked_children` and/or the per-child entry).
